nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.8
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be the field of constants of $\mathbf{K}$. It is enough to show that there is a unique $F$-derivation $\mathbb{D}'$ on $C^{1/p}$ extending $\mathbb{D}$. By Lemma \ref{deronc}(1), $C$ is an $F$-subfield of $K$. For $\mathbf{i}\in {\mathds{N}}^e$ and $a\in C^{1/p}$, we have the only option (as in \cite[Lemma 2.4]{Zieg2}): $$D'_{\mathbf{i}}(a):=(D_{p\mathbf{i}}(a^p))^{1/p}.$$ Clearly, each $D'_{\mathbf{i}}$ extends $D_{\mathbf{i}}$. We need to show that $\mathbb{D}'=(D'_{\mathbf{i}})_{\mathbf{i}\in {\mathds{N}}^e}$ is an $F$-derivation. By Lemma \ref{deronc}(2), the sequence of maps $$\mathbb{D}'':=(D_{p\mathbf{i}}(b))_{\mathbf{i}\in [p^m]^e}$$ is an $F[m-1]^{\mathrm{Fr}}$-derivation on $C$. It is easy to see that $\mathbb{D}'[m-1]$ coincides with $\mathbb{D}''$ ``transported'' to $C^{1/p}$ using the ring isomorphism $\mathrm{Fr}^{-1}_C:C\to C^{1/p}$. By Lemma \ref{transport}, $\mathbb{D}'[m-1]$ is an $F[m-1]$-derivation. Since it happens for all $m\in {\mathds{N}}$, we get that $\mathbb{D}'$ is an $F$-derivation.
nodes.statement_short: Extend D to C^{1/p} by D'_i(a)=D_{pi}(a^p)^{1/p} and check F[m-1]-iterativity via Lemma 3.31 and the transport lemma.

nodes.statement: The theory $F-\mathrm{DCF}$ is a model completion of the theory $F-\mathrm{DF}$ (so it eliminates quantifiers).
conclusions: The theory $F-\mathrm{DCF}$ is a model completion of the theory $F-\mathrm{DF}$ (so it eliminates quantifiers).

nodes.name: Why F-DF behaves better than g-DF
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item The extra property which makes the theory $F-\mathrm{DF}$ nicer than the theory $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DF}$ is the existence of the \emph{smallest} strict extensions (Proposition \ref{strictext}). It gives the amalgamation property for \emph{all} (i.e. not necessarily strict) $F$-fields (Proposition \ref{apf}) and the quantifier elimination for $F-\mathrm{DCF}$. \item In this context, quantifier elimination for $F-\mathrm{DCF}$ implies elimination of imaginaries for $F-\mathrm{DCF}$ exactly as in Section 4 of \cite{Zieg2}. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Smallest strict extensions give amalgamation for all F-fields, hence QE and elimination of imaginaries for F-DCF.

nodes.name: F-DCF as the union of the F[m]-DCF
nodes.statement: The theories $F[m]-\mathrm{DCF}$ form an increasing chain and we have $$F-\mathrm{DCF} = \bigcup_{m=1}^{\infty}F[m]-\mathrm{DCF}.$$
conclusions: The theories $F[m]-\mathrm{DCF}$ form an increasing chain
$$F-\mathrm{DCF} = \bigcup_{m=1}^{\infty}F[m]-\mathrm{DCF}.$$

nodes.name: Language L and theory SCF_{p,e}
nodes.statement: By $L$, we denote the language of $k$-algebras, and by $\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}$, the theory of separably closed $k$-algebras with the degree of imperfection $e$ in the language $L$ (so our notation does not reflect the dependence on $k$, we hope it will not cause any confusion).

nodes.name: Languages L^b and L_e^b
nodes.statement: We introduce two new languages (obtained after adding $e$ extra constant symbols): $$L^{\mathbf{b}}:=L\cup\lbrace b_1,\ldots,b_e\rbrace,\qquad L_e^{\mathbf{b}}:=L_e\cup\lbrace b_1,\ldots,b_e\rbrace.$$
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields

nodes.name: p-basis sentence beta
nodes.statement: Let $\beta$ be a sentence in the language $L^{\mathbf{b}}$ saying that $b_1,\ldots,b_e$ form a $p$-basis.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields

nodes.name: Theories SCF^b_{p,e} and F-DCF^b
nodes.statement: Now we add $\beta$ to the theory $\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}$ and to the theory $F-\mathrm{DCF}$ to obtain the theory $$\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}^{\mathbf{b}}:=\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}\;\cup\;\lbrace\beta\rbrace$$ in the language $L^{\mathbf{b}}$, and the theory $$F-\mathrm{DCF}^{\mathbf{b}}:=F-\mathrm{DCF}\;\cup\;\lbrace\beta\rbrace$$ in the language $L_e^{\mathbf{b}}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields

nodes.name: Separating transcendence basis of k(G)
nodes.statement: There are $x_1,\ldots,x_e\in k(G)$ algebraically independent over $k$ such that the field extension $k(x_1,\ldots,x_e)\subseteq k(G)$ is finite and separable.

conclusions: There are $x_1,\ldots,x_e\in k(G)$ algebraically independent over $k$ such that the field extension $k(x_1,\ldots,x_e)\subseteq k(G)$ is finite and separable.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.13
nodes.statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_e\in \mathcal{O}_G$ be a sequence of local parameters (see Example \ref{cangex}). By Example \ref{cangex}, \cite[30.6(ii)]{mat} and Proposition on page 276 of \cite{mat0}, $\{x_1,\ldots,x_e\}$ is a $p$-basis of $\mathcal{O}_G$, so it is also a $p$-basis of $k(G)$. Hence the field extension $k(x_1,\ldots,x_e)\subseteq k(G)$ is finite and separable.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Local parameters at the identity form a p-basis of O_G and hence of k(G).

nodes.name: Minimal polynomial H of a primitive element of k(G)
nodes.statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_e$ be as in Lemma \ref{finsep}. By Abel's theorem, there is $y\in k(G)$ such that $k(G)=k(x_1,\ldots,x_e,y)$. Let $H(X_1,\ldots,X_e,Y)\in k[X_1,\ldots,X_e,Y]$ be such that $H(x_1,\ldots,x_e,y)=0$ and the polynomial $H(x_1,\ldots,x_e,Y)$ is irreducible.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Choose y with k(G)=k(x,y) (Abel) and an irreducible polynomial relation H(x,y)=0.

nodes.name: Languages L^{b,c} and L_e^{b,c}
nodes.statement: We need to add one more constant to the languages we consider to obtain the following languages: $$L^{{\mathbf{b}},c}:=L\cup\lbrace b_1,\ldots,b_e,c\rbrace,\qquad L_e^{{\mathbf{b}},c}:=L_e\cup\lbrace b_1,\ldots,b_e,c\rbrace.$$

nodes.name: Axiom gamma
nodes.statement: Formally, we specify one more axiom $\gamma$ in the language $L^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$ $$\gamma:=\ \ \beta \ \wedge \ (H(b_1,\ldots,b_e,c)=0).$$
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields

nodes.name: Theories SCF^{b,c}_{p,e} and F-DCF^{b,c}
nodes.statement: We define the following theories. $$\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}:=\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}\;\cup\;\lbrace \gamma\rbrace,\ \ F-\mathrm{DCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}:=F-\mathrm{DCF}\;\cup\;\lbrace \gamma\rbrace .$$
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields

nodes.name: Bi-interpretability of G-DCF with SCF
nodes.statement: The theory $G-\mathrm{DCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$ is an extension by definitions of the theory $\mathrm{SCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}_{p,e}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
conclusions: The theory $G-\mathrm{DCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$ is an extension by definitions of the theory $\mathrm{SCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}_{p,e}$.
nodes.statement_short: With constants for a p-basis and a generator of k(G), G-DCF is an extension by definitions of SCF_{p,e}.
nodes.label: biin

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.14
nodes.statement: Take $x_1,\ldots,x_e\in k(G)$ as in Lemma \ref{finsep}, denote $(x_1,\ldots,x_e)$ by $\mathbf{x}$ and let $y\in k(G)$ be separable algebraic over $k(\mathbf{x})$ such that $k(\mathbf{x},y)=k(G)$ (such $y$ exists by Lemma \ref{finsep} and Abel's theorem). Then for any $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}\in {\mathds{N}}^e$, there are polynomials $F_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}},H_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}\in k[\mathbf{X},Y]$ such that for the canonical $F$-derivation $\mathbb{D}^{F}=(D_{\mathbf{j}}^F)_{\mathbf{j}\in\mathbb{N}^e}$ on $k(G)$, we have $$D_{\mathbf{j}}^F(\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{i}})=\frac{F_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{x},y)}{H_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{x},y)}\in k(G).$$ We describe now an extension by definitions of the theory $\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$ coinciding with the theory $G-\mathrm{DCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$. To ease the notation, we will also denote by $\mathbf{b}$ the tuple (of constant symbols or elements of a model) $(b_1,\ldots,b_e)$. Take $\mathbf{j}=(j_1,\ldots,j_e)\in\mathbb{N}^e$, for every $n\geqslant \max\lbrace j_1,\ldots,j_e\rbrace$ we add to the theory $\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$ the following defining axiom \begin{equation}\tag{$\clubsuit$} D_{\mathbf{j}}(x)=y \leftrightarrow \left(\exists^{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\; \alpha_{\mathbf{i}}\right) \left(x=\sum\limits_{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\alpha_{\mathbf{i}}^{p^n}\mathbf{b}^{\mathbf{i}} \;\wedge\; y=\sum\limits_{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\alpha_{\mathbf{i}}^{p^n}\frac{F_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{b},c)}{H_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{b},c)} \right). \end{equation} Take any $(K,\mathbf{b},c)\models \mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$. It is not hard to verify that the defining axioms (\ref{scfD}) determine well-defined functions on $K$. The axioms $\beta,\gamma$ guarantee that $$k(\mathbf{b},c)\cong_k k(G)$$ and that $\mathbb{D}:=(D_{\mathbf{j}})_{\mathbf{j}\in {\mathds{N}}^e}$ restricted to $k(\mathbf{b},c)$ corresponds to the canonical $G$-derivation on $k(G)$. Because $\mathbf{b}$ is a $p$-basis of $K$, the extension $k(\mathbf{b})\subseteq K$ is \'{e}tale (see \cite[Theorem 26.8]{mat}). Hence the extension $k(\mathbf{b},c)\subseteq K$ is also \'{e}tale. Due to Proposition \ref{etalehs}, we can extend the canonical $G$-derivation from $k(G)$ to the field $K$. Let $\mathbb{D}'=\left(D'_{\mathbf{j}}\right)_{\mathbf{j}\in\mathbb{N}^e}$ denote the $G$-derivation on $K$ extending the canonical $G$-derivation on $k(G)$. Note that $D'_{\mathbf{j}}(x)=D_{\mathbf{j}}(x)$ for every $x\in K$, hence $\mathbb{D}'=\mathbb{D}$. Moreover the canonical $G$-derivation on $k(G)$ is strict, so also $\mathbb{D}'|_{k(\mathbf{b},c)}$ is strict. Lemma \ref{constantdisjoint} implies that $\mathbb{D}'=\mathbb{D}$ is strict, so $(K,\mathbb{D},\mathbf{b},c)\models G-\mathrm{DCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$.

nodes.statement_short: Define each D_j by expanding x in the p^n-power basis of b and applying the canonical G-derivation formulas; étaleness of k(b,c) ⊆ K and Lemma 3.22 show this is the unique strict G-derivation.

nodes.statement: \tag{$\clubsuit$} D_{\mathbf{j}}(x)=y \leftrightarrow \left(\exists^{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\; \alpha_{\mathbf{i}}\right) \left(x=\sum\limits_{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\alpha_{\mathbf{i}}^{p^n}\mathbf{b}^{\mathbf{i}} \;\wedge\; y=\sum\limits_{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\alpha_{\mathbf{i}}^{p^n}\frac{F_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{b},c)}{H_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{b},c)} \right).

nodes.name: Constant c often unnecessary
nodes.statement: In many cases, the theory $G-\mathrm{DCF}^{\mathbf{b}}$ is an extension by definitions of the theory $\mathrm{SCF}^{{\mathbf{b}}}_{p,e}$, so in such cases the constant symbol $c$ is not necessary. For example, it is the case for $G$ being the group of Witt vectors, see \cite{Hoff2}.

nodes.name: Bi-interpretability for arbitrary formal groups
nodes.statement: It is unclear to us how to proceed in the case of an arbitrary formal group $F$. The crucial question is whether the canonical derivation on $k((\mathbf{X}))$ can be restricted to $k(\mathbf{X})$ or to $k(\mathbf{X})^{\mathrm{sep}}$.

nodes.name: Isomorphic formal groups give definitionally equivalent theories
nodes.statement: Assume that $F_1$ and $F_2$ are one-dimensional formal group laws over $k$ such that $F_1\cong F_2$. Then the theory $F_1-\mathrm{DCF}$ is an extension by definitions of the theory $F_2-\mathrm{DCF}$.

assumptions: Assume that $F_1$ and $F_2$ are one-dimensional formal group laws over $k$ such that $F_1\cong F_2$.
conclusions: the theory $F_1-\mathrm{DCF}$ is an extension by definitions of the theory $F_2-\mathrm{DCF}$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.16
nodes.statement: Let $f\in Xk\llbracket X\rrbracket$ be an isomorphism between $F_1$ and $F_2$. For any $F_1$-derivation $\mathbb{D}:K\to K\llbracket X\rrbracket$, the following composition \begin{equation*} \xymatrix{K \ar[r]^{\mathbb{D}} & K\llbracket X\rrbracket \ar[r]^{\mathrm{ev}_f} & K\llbracket X\rrbracket} \end{equation*} is an $F_2$-derivation. It is easy to see that for each positive integer $n$, there are $c_{n,1},\ldots,c_{n,n}\in k$ such that if $\mathbb{D}=(D_i)_{i\in {\mathds{N}}}$ then the corresponding $F_2$-derivation $\mathrm{ev}_f\circ \mathbb{D}$ is of the form $$(\mathrm{id},c_{1,1}D_1,c_{2,1}D_1+c_{2,2}D_2,\ldots),$$ hence the result follows.

nodes.statement_short: Compose with evaluation at the isomorphism f; the new operators are k-linear triangular combinations of the old ones.

nodes.statement: Suppose that $F$ is a one-dimensional formal group law over an algebraically closed field $k$ (in particular $e=1$). Then the theory $F-\mathrm{DCF}^{\mathbf{b}}$ is an extension by definitions of the theory $\mathrm{SCF}^{\mathbf{b}}_{p,1}$.

assumptions: Suppose that $F$ is a one-dimensional formal group law over an algebraically closed field $k$ (in particular $e=1$).
conclusions: the theory $F-\mathrm{DCF}^{\mathbf{b}}$ is an extension by definitions of the theory $\mathrm{SCF}^{\mathbf{b}}_{p,1}$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.17
nodes.statement: By \cite[Thm. 4.3]{HK2}, there is a formal group law $\widetilde{F}$ over $k$ such that $F\cong \widetilde{F}$ and the canonical $\widetilde{F}$-derivation restricts to $k[X]$. By Lemma \ref{isodef}, we can assume that $F=\widetilde{F}$. We can repeat now the proof of Theorem \ref{biin} (and we do not need to worry about the extra constant $c$).

nodes.statement_short: Replace F by an isomorphic law whose canonical derivation restricts to k[X] (HK2, Thm 4.3), then repeat the proof of Theorem 4.14.

nodes.name: Algebraic closedness of k is harmless
nodes.statement: Passing from the base field $k$ to its algebraic closure expands the language with extra constants. But any existentially closed $F$-field is separably closed, so its field of absolute constants contains $k^{\mathrm{alg}}$. Hence such an expansion is not important for the theories we consider, since the models of $F-\mathrm{DCF}$ in the language with constants for elements of $k$ are the same as models of $F-\mathrm{DCF}$ in the language with constants for elements of $k^{\mathrm{alg}}$. Therefore, the assumption in Theorem \ref{onedimext} that $k$ is algebraically closed is harmless.

nodes.name: Functor D
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be the functor from the category of $K$-algebras to the category of $K[\mathbf{v}_m]$-algebras defined in the following way: $$\mathcal{D}(R)=R\otimes_{K,\mathbb{D}}K[\mathbf{v}_m].$$

nodes.name: Prolongation functor nabla
nodes.statement: The functor $\mathcal{D}$ considered as a functor from $K$-algebras to $K$-algebras has a left-adjoint functor $\nabla$ which extends to $K$-schemes. A crucial natural bijection is the following one: $$(\nabla V)(R)\longleftrightarrow V(\mathcal{D}(R)).$$

nodes.statement: For any $K$-scheme $V$ we have a (non-algebraic!) map $$\mathbb{D}_{V}:V(K)\to V(\mathcal{D}(K))=\nabla V(K)$$ induced by the $K$-algebra homomorphism $\mathbb{D}:K\to K[\mathbf{v}_m]=\mathcal{D}(K)$.

nodes.name: Extension of D to polynomial rings
nodes.statement: For any positive integer $n$, our HS-derivation $\mathbb{D}$ naturally extends to the following HS-derivation $$\left(D_{\mathbf{j}}:K[X_1,\ldots,X_n]\to K[X_1^{(\mathbf{i})},\ldots,X_n^{(\mathbf{i})}\ |\ \mathbf{i}\in[p^m]^e\ ]\right)_{\mathbf{j}\in[p^m]^e},\ \ \mathbb{D}_{\mathbf{j}}(X)=X^{(\mathbf{j})},$$ where $X_k^{(\mathbf{0})}=X_k$ and for $\mathbf{j}\neq \mathbf{0}$, $X_k^{(\mathbf{j})}$ is a new variable.

nodes.name: Ring K{X_1,...,X_n}
nodes.statement: We will use the following notation $$K\{X_1,\ldots,X_n\}:=K[X_1^{(\mathbf{i})},\ldots,X_n^{(\mathbf{i})}\ |\ \mathbf{i}\in[p^m]^e\ ].$$

nodes.name: Explicit description of nabla and D_V
nodes.statement: If $R=K[X_1,\ldots,X_n]/I$, then $\nabla(R)=K\{X_1,\ldots,X_n\}/(\mathbb{D}(I))$. Hence, for an affine variety $V=\mathrm{Spec}(R)$, the variety $\nabla(V)$ is defined by the ideal $(\mathbb{D}(I))$ and $\mathbb{D}_V$ is given in coordinates as the $n$-th Cartesian product of $\mathbb{D}$ (considered as a map from $K$ to $K^{p^{me}}$).
conclusions: $\nabla(R)=K\{X_1,\ldots,X_n\}/(\mathbb{D}(I))$

nodes.name: c_n
nodes.statement: Let $c_n$ denote $c_{\mathds{A}^{np^{me}}}$.

nodes.name: Explicit formula for c_n
nodes.statement: For every $(b_{\mathbf{i},1},\ldots,b_{\mathbf{i},n})_{\mathbf{i}\in [p^m]^e}\in K^{np^{me}}$ we have $$c_n\left((b_{\mathbf{i},1},\ldots,b_{\mathbf{i},n})_{\mathbf{i}\in [p^m]^e}\right)= \left(\sum\limits_{\mathbf{k}\in[p^m]^e}c_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}^{\mathbf{k}}b_{\mathbf{k},1},\ldots, \sum\limits_{\mathbf{k}\in[p^m]^e}c_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}^{\mathbf{k}}b_{\mathbf{k},n}\right)_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}\in [p^m]^e},$$ where $c_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}^{\mathbf{k}}$ are the ``structural constants'' from Remark \ref{gderint2}.
nodes.statement_short: c_n acts coordinatewise by the structural constants of the comultiplication.

nodes.name: Prolongations of points in extensions
nodes.statement: Let $V$ be a $K$-scheme and suppose that $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq(L,\mathbb{D}')$ is an extension of $m$-truncated $e$-dimensional HS-fields. Then for any $a\in V(L)$, we have $\mathbb{D}'_V(a)\in\nabla V(L)$.
assumptions: Let $V$ be a $K$-scheme and suppose that $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq(L,\mathbb{D}')$ is an extension of $m$-truncated $e$-dimensional HS-fields.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: It is enough to notice that if $\mathbb{D}'$ extends $\mathbb{D}$, then the $k$-algebra map $\mathbb{D}':L\to \mathcal{D}(L)$ is $K$-linear.
nodes.statement_short: The extension map L -> D(L) is K-linear.

nodes.name: Justification of Lemma 5.3 (prose)
nodes.statement: The following lemma corresponds to \cite[Lemma 1.1(ii)]{K3} and is a direct consequence of the $\mathfrak{g}$-iterativity condition.
nodes.statement_short: Direct consequence of the g-iterativity condition, as in K3 Lemma 1.1(ii).

nodes.name: Iterativity in terms of nabla
nodes.statement: For any $K$-scheme $V$ we have the following: $$\mathbb{D}_{\nabla(V)}\circ \mathbb{D}_V=c_V\circ \mathbb{D}_V.$$
conclusions: $$\mathbb{D}_{\nabla(V)}\circ \mathbb{D}_V=c_V\circ \mathbb{D}_V.$$

nodes.name: Saturated field Omega
nodes.statement: Let us fix a $|K|^+$-saturated algebraically closed field $\Omega$ containing $K$.

nodes.name: Points b_0, b and loci V, W
nodes.statement: Let $b_0\in\Omega^n$, $b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{p^{me}-1})\in\Omega^{np^{me}}$ and we set $$V=\mathrm{locus}_K(b_0),\ \ \ W=\mathrm{locus}_K(b).$$

nodes.name: Justification of Lemma 5.4 (prose)
nodes.statement: As in \cite[Lemma 3.3]{K3}, we can show the following.
nodes.statement_short: As in K3, Lemma 3.3.

nodes.name: Extending D along a prolongation point
nodes.statement: If $b\in \nabla V(\Omega)$ and $K(b_0)=K(b)$, then there is an $m$-truncated $e$-dimensional HS-derivation $\mathbb{D}'$ on $K(b)$ extending $\mathbb{D}$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$.
conclusions: there is an $m$-truncated $e$-dimensional HS-derivation $\mathbb{D}'$ on $K(b)$ extending $\mathbb{D}$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$
nodes.label: nablaext

nodes.name: Justification of Lemma 5.5 (prose)
nodes.statement: Finally, we obtain the following lemma by using Lemmas \ref{nablaL}, \ref{gitnabla}, \ref{nablaext} (as in \cite{K3}).
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemmas 5.2, 5.3 and 5.4 as in K3.

nodes.name: Criterion for g-field extensions via c_n
nodes.statement: The following are equivalent. \begin{enumerate} \item There is a $\mathfrak{g}$-field extension $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq(K(b),\mathbb{D}')$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$. \item There is a $\mathfrak{g}$-field extension $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq(L,\mathbb{D}')$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$. \item $c_{n}(W)\subseteq \nabla(W)$. \end{enumerate}
conclusions: There is a $\mathfrak{g}$-field extension $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq(K(b),\mathbb{D}')$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$.
There is a $\mathfrak{g}$-field extension $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq(L,\mathbb{D}')$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$.
$c_{n}(W)\subseteq \nabla(W)$.
nodes.statement_short: A g-field extension realizing b as the prolongation of b_0 exists iff c_n(W) ⊆ ∇(W).
nodes.label: cVW

nodes.name: Geometric axioms for g-DCF
nodes.statement: {\bf Geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$} \begin{enumerate} \item The field $K$ is separably closed. \item For each positive integer $n$, suppose that $V\subseteq {\mathbb A}^n$ and $W\subseteq \nabla(V)$ are absolutely irreducible $K$-varieties, and $Z$ is a proper $K$-subvariety of $W$. If $W$ projects generically onto $V$, and $c_{V}(W)\subseteq \nabla (W)$, then there is $a\in V(K)$ such that $\mathbb{D}_{V}(a)\in W(K)\setminus Z(K)$.
nodes.statement_short: K is separably closed and every suitable pair V, W ⊆ ∇(V) with c_V(W) ⊆ ∇(W) has a K-point a with D_V(a) generic in W.

nodes.name: The geometric axioms are first-order
nodes.statement: These axioms are first-order, since for a separably closed field $K$, any $K$-irreducible variety is absolutely irreducible.
conclusions: These axioms are first-order

nodes.name: Geometric axiomatization of existentially closed g-fields
nodes.statement: The $\mathfrak{g}$-field $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is an existentially closed $\mathfrak{g}$-field if and only if $(K,\mathbb{D})$ satisfies the geometric axioms above.
conclusions: is an existentially closed $\mathfrak{g}$-field if and only if $(K,\mathbb{D})$ satisfies the geometric axioms above
nodes.label: ggeo

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.6
nodes.statement:
Assume that $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is an existentially closed $\mathfrak{g}$-field. Then by Proposition ef{etalegext}, $K$ is separably closed (since a separable algebraic field extension is '{e}tale). Take any $K$-irreducible $K$-varieties $V\subseteq \mathbb{A}^n$, $W\subseteq 
abla(V)$ and $Z\subsetneq W$. If $W$ projects generically onto $V$ then there is $b_0\in\Omega^n$ and $b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{p^{me}-1})\in\Omega^{np^{me}}$ such that $V=\mathrm{locus}_K(b_0)$ and $W=\mathrm{locus}_K(b)$. Since $c_V(W)\subseteq 
abla(W)$, Lemma ef{cVW} implies that there exists a $\mathfrak{g}$-field extension $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq (K(b),\mathbb{D}')$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$. We have $$\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b\in W(K(b))\setminus Z(K(b))$$ and $b_0\in V(K(b))$. Since $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is existentially closed, there is $b_0'\in V(K)$ such that $\mathbb{D}_V(b'_0)\in W(K)\setminus Z(K)$. \ \ Assume now that $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is a model of the ``geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$'' and let $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq (L,\mathbb{D}')$ be an extension of $\mathfrak{g}$-fields. Take any quantifier-free formula $\varphi(x_0,\ldots,x_{p^{me}-1})$ over $K$ (in the language of fields), where each $x_i$ is an $n$-tuple of variables for an arbitrary (but fixed) positive integer $n$. Suppose that $(L,\mathbb{D}')\models (\exists x_0)\varphi(\mathbb{D}'(x_0))$. Take $b_0\in L^n$ such that $(L,\mathbb{D}')\models\varphi(\mathbb{D}'(b_0))$ and set $$V=\mathrm{locus}_K(b_0),\ \ b=\mathbb{D}_V'(b_0),\ \ W=\mathrm{locus}_K(b),\ \ Z_0=\lbrace d\in W\;\;|\;\; 
eg\varphi(d)brace.$$ Let $Z$ denote the intersection of all $K$-subvarieties of $W$ containing $Z_0$. Clearly $b\in W(L)\setminus Z(L)$ and the second condition of Lemma ef{cVW} is satisfied, so $c_{V}(W)\subseteq 
abla(W)$. Hence all the assumptions of the ``geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$'' hold. Therefore there is $b_0'\in V(K)$ such that $\mathbb{D}(b_0')\in W(K)\setminus Z(K)$ and $(K,\mathbb{D})\models (\exists x_0)\varphi(\mathbb{D}(x_0))$.
nodes.statement_short: Both directions via Lemma 5.5: an e.c. field realizes the generic point of W; conversely a witness in an extension yields varieties V, W, Z to which the axioms apply.

nodes.name: Section 4 not needed for Theorem 5.6
nodes.statement: Note that the results of Section \ref{secmc} are not used in the proof of Theorem \ref{ggeo} which suggests a possibility of generalizations, e.g. to the context of $\mathcal{D}$-fields from \cite{MS}.
nodes.label: gremark

nodes.name: Geometric axioms for F-DCF
nodes.statement:
By Theorem ef{chain}, the geometric axioms for $F-\mathrm{DCF}$ are given as the union (over $m$) of the geometric axioms for $F[m]-\mathrm{DCF}$. We state these axioms explicitly below, where $
abla_m$ denotes the functor $
abla$ with respect to $\mathbb{D}[m]$ (similarly for $c_m$). \ \ { f Geometric axioms for $F-\mathrm{DCF}$}  egin{enumerate} \item The field $K$ is separably closed. \item For any positive integers $n,m$, suppose that $V\subseteq {\mathbb A}^n$ and $W\subseteq 
abla_m(V)$ are absolutely irreducible $K$-varieties, and $Z$ is a proper $K$-subvariety of $W$. If $W$ projects generically onto $V$, and $c_{m,V}(W)\subseteq 
abla_m(W)$, then there is $a\in V(K)$ such that $\mathbb{D}[m]_{V}(a)\in W(K)\setminus Z(K)$.
nodes.statement_short: Union over m of the geometric axioms for F[m]-DCF, stated with ∇_m and c_m.

nodes.name: Geometric axiomatization of existentially closed F-fields
nodes.statement: The $F$-field $\mathbf{K}$ is an existentially closed $F$-field if and only if $\mathbf{K}$ is a model of the geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$.
conclusions: is an existentially closed $F$-field if and only if $\mathbf{K}$ is a model of the geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$
nodes.label: fgeo

nodes.name: Role of Theorem 4.12 in Theorem 5.8
nodes.statement: Unlike in the proof of Theorem \ref{ggeo}, the results of Section \ref{secmc} \emph{are} used for the proof of Theorem \ref{fgeo}, since Theorem \ref{chain} is necessary for the geometric axiomatization and the proof of Theorem \ref{chain} requires the algebraic axiomatizations of $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$ and $F-\mathrm{DCF}$. However, one can also prove Theorem \ref{chain} (but for a limited class of formal groups $F$ only) in another fashion as it was done in \cite{K3} for $F=\widehat{\mathbb{G}_{\rm{a}}^e}$. This approach will be discussed in Section \ref{secgtup}.
nodes.label: fremark

nodes.name: Model theory of iterative D-fields in positive characteristic
nodes.statement: One could wonder whether our techniques may be generalized to include the case of iterative $\underline{\mathcal{D}}$-fields of positive characteristic.

nodes.name: Canonical G-tuple
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb{D}$ be a $G[m]$-derivation on $K$. A subset $B\subseteq K$ is called a \emph{canonical $G$-tuple}, if $|B|=e$ and there is a $G[m]$-embedding $(k(G),\mathbb{D}[m]^G)\to \mathbf{K}$ such that $B$ is the image of the set of canonical parameters of $G$, where $\mathbb{D}[m]^G$ is the canonical $G[m]$-derivation from Example \ref{cangex}.
nodes.statement_short: An e-element set that is the image of the canonical parameters of G under a G[m]-embedding of (k(G), canonical derivation).
nodes.label: defpbasis

nodes.name: Canonical G-tuples are p-bases
nodes.statement: If $\mathbf{L}$ is strict and of imperfection degree $e$, then any canonical $G$-tuple in $L$ is a $p$-basis. For $G=\mathbb{G}_{\rm{a}}^e$, we recover the notion of a \emph{canonical $p$-basis} from \cite{Zieg2}.
nodes.label: geotuple

nodes.name: Existence of canonical G-tuples
nodes.statement: We say that \emph{canonical $G$-tuples exist} if for any $m$ and any separably closed $G[m]$-field $\mathbf{L}$, whenever $[L:C_L]=p^e$, there is a canonical $G$-tuple in $L$.
nodes.statement_short: Every separably closed G[m]-field with [L:C_L]=p^e contains a canonical G-tuple.
nodes.label: existence

nodes.name: Generalizations and known existence results for canonical G-tuples
nodes.statement: \begin{enumerate} \item Definition \ref{defpbasis} can be phrased in a (much) greater generality using group scheme actions. Let $\mathfrak{G}_0$ be a group subscheme of a group scheme $\mathfrak{G}$. Assume that $\mathfrak{G}_0$ acts (as a group scheme) on a scheme $V$. We say that this action has a \emph{canonical $\mathfrak{G}$-basis}, if there is an $\mathfrak{G}_0$-invariant morphism $V\to \mathfrak{G}$ such that the induced map $$V\to \mathfrak{G}\times_{\mathfrak{G}/\mathfrak{G}_0}V/\mathfrak{G}_0$$ is an isomorphism. \item The existence of canonical $\mathbb{G}_a^e$-tuples is shown in \cite{Zieg2} and the existence of canonical $\mathbb{G}_m$-tuples is shown in \cite{HK1}. Combining these results, one can show the existence of canonical $G$-tuples for $G$ of the form $\mathbb{G}_a^e\times\mathbb{G}_m^f$. \item We do not attack here the problem of the \emph{existence} of canonical $G$-tuples for a given algebraic group $G$. This will be done in \cite{Hoff1} (as well as possible applications to the notion of ``$G$-thinness''). \item The existence of canonical $G$-tuples implies (\emph{strong}) \emph{integrability} of $G$-derivations, as in (morally) \cite{Mats1} or as in \cite{HK1} (see also \cite{Tyc}) \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: greater

nodes.name: Canonical G-tuples give another proof of Theorem 4.12
nodes.statement: The existence of canonical $G$-tuples gives rather directly (see \cite[Thm. 2.3]{K3}) another proof of Theorem \ref{chain} which is the only ingredient needed in Section \ref{secaxioms} requiring specific differential-algebraic arguments.

nodes.name: Reduce to inductive step
nodes.statement: The proof goes almost exactly as in \cite[theorem 27.2]{mat}, so we will just sketch the main inductive step which makes clear how the \'{e}tale assumption is used. We apply the induction on the truncation degree.
nodes.statement_short: Follow Matsumura 27.2; induct on the truncation degree.

nodes.name: Inductive hypothesis and lifting diagram
nodes.statement: Assume that for $l\in {\mathds{N}}$ (resp. $l<m$) we have extended $\mathbb{D}[l]$ to an $l$-truncated $e$-dimensional HS-derivation $\mathbb{D}':=(D'_{\mathbf{i}})_{\mathbf{i}<[p^l]^e}$ on $S$. Consider the following diagram \begin{equation*} \xymatrixcolsep{2.5pc}\xymatrixrowsep{1.5pc}\xymatrix{& S[\mathbf{X}]/(X_1^{p^l},\ldots,X_e^{p^l}) & \\ S \ar[ur]^-{\mathbb{D}'} \ar@{-->}[rr] & & S[\mathbf{X}]/(X_1^{p^{l+1}},\ldots,X_e^{p^{l+1}}) \ar[ul]_{\pi} \\ & R \ar[ul]^{f} \ar[ur]_{\mathbb{D}[l+1]} & } \end{equation*} where $\pi$ is the quotient map.
nodes.statement_short: Assume D[l] extended to S and set up the lifting diagram.

nodes.name: Kernel is nilpotent
nodes.statement: Then $(\ker \pi)^{e+1}=0$, so $\ker(\pi)$ is nilpotent.
nodes.statement_short: The kernel of the truncation map is nilpotent.

nodes.name: Étale lifting
nodes.statement: Since the map $R\to S$ is \'{e}tale, we get a unique $k$-algebra map $$S\to S[\mathbf{X}]/(X_1^{p^{l+1}},\ldots,X_e^{p^{l+1}})$$ completing the diagram above.
nodes.statement_short: Étaleness gives the unique lift to level l+1.

nodes.name: Form of the comultiplication
nodes.statement: It is clear for $\text{\textbf{i}}=\mathbf{0}$ or $\text{\textbf{j}}=\mathbf{0}$, so we assume that $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}\neq \mathbf{0}$. By a truncated version of the formula \cite[(14.1.1)]{Hazew}, we have (in the notation of Remark \ref{gderint}) $$c(\mathbf{w}_m)=\mathbf{w}_m+\mathbf{v}_m+\mathbf{s}_m,$$ where $\mathbf{s}_m=(S_1,\ldots,S_e)$ for some $S_1,\ldots,S_e$ belonging to the ideal $(\mathbf{w}_m\cdot \mathbf{v}_m)$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to i,j nonzero; comultiplication is w+v+s with s in (w·v).

nodes.name: Iterativity identity
nodes.statement: Therefore for every $r\in R$ we have $$\sum_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}} D_{\mathbf{j}}D_{\mathbf{i}}(r)\mathbf{v}_m^{\mathbf{i}}\mathbf{w}_m^{\mathbf{j}}= \sum_{\mathbf{k}} D_{\mathbf{k}}(r)(\mathbf{w}_m+\mathbf{v}_m+\mathbf{s}_m)^{\mathbf{k}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Write the iterativity identity in coordinates.

nodes.name: Compare coefficients
nodes.statement: We get the result by comparing the coefficients at $\mathbf{v}_m^{\mathbf{i}}\mathbf{w}_m^{\mathbf{j}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare coefficients of v^i w^j.

nodes.name: Dependence gives C-linearity
nodes.statement: Assume that $x_l=c_1x_1+\ldots+c_{l-1}x_{l-1}$ for some $c_1,\ldots, c_{l-1}\in C$. By Lemma \ref{absconst}, each $D_{\mathbf{i}}$ is $C$-linear.
nodes.statement_short: Assume a dependence; by Lemma 3.16 each D_i is C-linear.

nodes.name: Rank drops
nodes.statement: Hence we obtain that the rank of our Wronskian matrix is smaller than $l$ as in the standard case (see \cite[Thm. II.1]{kol1}).
nodes.statement_short: Hence the Wronskian has rank < l.

nodes.name: Rank r < l
nodes.statement: Let the rank of the matrix $\big(D_{\mathbf{i}}(x_j)\big)_{\mathbf{i}\in [p]^e,j\leqslant l}$ be equal to $r<l$. After reordering $x_1,\ldots,x_l$, we may assume that the matrix $\big(D_{\mathbf{i}}(x_j)\big)_{\mathbf{i}\in [p]^e,j\leqslant r}$ has rank $r$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume rank r < l and reorder so the first r columns have rank r.

nodes.name: Dependence relation (*)
nodes.statement: Therefore there exist $\lambda_1,\ldots, \lambda_{r+1}\in K$, not all equal to $0$, such that for each tuple $\mathbf{k}$ we have \begin{equation} \sum\limits_{s=1}^{r+1}\lambda_sD_{\mathbf{k}}(x_s)=0.\tag{$*$} \end{equation} \noindent Reordering and dividing by $c_{r+1}$ if need be, we may assume that $c_{r+1}=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Get a nontrivial relation (*) among the first r+1 columns, normalized.

nodes.name: Structural constants
nodes.statement: By Remark \ref{gderint2}, there are $c_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}^{\mathbf{k}}\in C$ such that for all tuples $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}$ we have $$D_{\mathbf{j}}\circ D_{\mathbf{i}}=\sum_{\mathbf{k}}c_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}^{\mathbf{k}}D_{\mathbf{k}}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Use the structural constants of g-iterativity.

nodes.name: Coefficients are constants
nodes.statement: Hence for $\mathbf{1}:=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ and every tuple $\mathbf{i}$ we get (using $(*)$ with $\mathbf{k}=\mathbf{1}$ for the last equality) \begin{IEEEeqnarray*}{rCl} 0 & = & \sum\limits_{s=1}^{r+1}D_{\mathbf{1}}(\lambda_s)D_{\mathbf{i}}(x_s)+\sum\limits_{s=1}^{r+1}\lambda_sD_{\mathbf{1}}(D_{\mathbf{i}}(x_s)) \\ & = & \sum\limits_{s=1}^{r}D_{\mathbf{1}}(\lambda_s)D_{\mathbf{i}}(x_s)+\sum\limits_{\mathbf{l}}c_{\mathbf{1},\mathbf{i}}^{\mathbf{l}}\sum\limits_{s=1}^{r+1}\lambda_sD_{\mathbf{l}}(x_s) \\ & = & \sum\limits_{s=1}^{r}D_{\mathbf{1}}(\lambda_s)D_{\mathbf{i}}(x_s). \end{IEEEeqnarray*} Thus $D_{(1,0,\ldots,0)}(\lambda_s)=0$ for every $s\leqslant r$. After similar reasoning for the derivations $D_{(0,1,0,\ldots,0)},\ldots,D_{(0,\ldots,0,1)}$ we get $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{r+1}\in C$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply D_1 to (*) and use minimality to get D_1(λ_s)=0; similarly for the other derivations.

nodes.name: Linear dependence
nodes.statement: By setting $\mathbf{k}=\mathbf{0}$ in $(*)$, we obtain that $x_1,\ldots,x_l$ are linearly dependent over $C$.
nodes.statement_short: k=0 in (*) gives linear dependence over C.

nodes.name: Rank bound
nodes.statement: Let $l=p^e+1$ and $x_1,\ldots,x_l\in K$. The rank of the corresponding Wronskian matrix from Proposition \ref{wronskian} is at most $p^e$, since there are only $p^e$ operators of the form $D_{\mathbf{i}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Any p^e+1 elements give a Wronskian of rank at most p^e.

nodes.name: Apply Wronskian theorem
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{wronskian}, $x_1,\ldots,x_l$ are linearly dependent over $C$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence they are dependent over C.

nodes.name: Part (1)
nodes.statement: For $(1)$, we apply Lemma \ref{wronskian} as in the standard case (see \cite[Cor. 1, p. 87]{kol1}).
nodes.statement_short: Linear disjointness via the Wronskian criterion.

nodes.name: Part (2) and easy direction of (3)
nodes.statement: The item $(2)$ follows directly from $(1)$ using \cite[Thm. 26.4]{mat}. \\ The right-to-left implication in $(3)$ is clear (and only the condition $L^p\cap K=K^p$ is used).
nodes.statement_short: Separability from (1) and Matsumura 26.4; right-to-left of (3) is clear.

nodes.name: Étale consequences
nodes.statement: For the left-to-right implication, the \'{e}tale assumption implies that $[L:L^p]=[K:K^p]$ and $KL^p=L$.
nodes.statement_short: Étaleness gives [L:L^p]=[K:K^p] and KL^p=L.

nodes.name: Degree computation
nodes.statement: Since $L^p\subseteq C_L$, by $(1)$ (used for the second equality below) we get $$[L:L^p]=[K:K^p]=[KC_L:C_L]=[L:C_L].$$
nodes.statement_short: Using (1), compute [L:L^p]=[L:C_L].

nodes.name: L is strict
nodes.statement: Since $[L:L^p]$ is finite, we get $C_L=L^p$.
nodes.statement_short: Finiteness gives C_L=L^p.

nodes.name: First-order operators
nodes.statement: We introduce the following notation: $$\partial^F_1=D_{(1,0,\ldots,0)},\ldots,\partial^F_e=D_{(0,\ldots,0,1)}.$$
nodes.statement_short: Name the first-order operators ∂^F_i.

nodes.name: Chain rule (*)
nodes.statement: Let $i\leqslant e$ and $f\in K$. By the chain rule, we get \begin{equation} \partial^F_i(f)=\Big(\frac{\partial F_i}{\partial Y_j}(\mathbf{X},0)\Big)_{i,j}\cdot \Big(\frac{\partial f}{\partial X_1},\ldots,\frac{\partial f}{\partial X_e}\Big).\tag{$*$} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule expresses ∂^F_i(f) via a Jacobian.

nodes.name: Jacobian invertible
nodes.statement: Let $J$ denote the Jacobian matrix appearing in $(*)$. Then $J$ is the matrix of the derivative (at $\mathbf{0}$) of the formal map which is the ``$F$-multiplication by $\mathbf{X}$''. Since this formal map is (formally) invertible, the matrix $J$ is non-singular.
nodes.statement_short: The Jacobian of F-multiplication is invertible.

nodes.name: Constants are p-th powers
nodes.statement: Therefore $f$ belongs to the field of constants if and only if $\frac{\partial f}{\partial X_i}=0$ for each $i$. The latter condition occurs if and only if $f$ is a $p$-th power, so the result is proved.
nodes.statement_short: So constants are exactly the p-th powers.

nodes.name: Existence of quotient
nodes.statement: For $(1)$, we quote \cite[Thm 1(A), p. 111]{MuAbel}.
nodes.statement_short: Quote Mumford's quotient theorem.

nodes.name: Quotient ring
nodes.statement: By the proof of \cite[Thm 1(A), p. 111]{MuAbel} we have $V/\mathfrak{g}=\mathrm{Spec}(C')$ where $$C'=\{r\in R\ |\ \mathbb{D}(r)=r\}.$$ Clearly $C'$ coincides with $C_{\mathbb{D}}$ giving $(2)$.
nodes.statement_short: The quotient ring is the ring of invariants = absolute constants.

nodes.name: Constants as quotient
nodes.statement: We work on the level of group scheme actions. By Theorem \ref{quotient}(2), we have $\mathrm{Spec}(C)=\mathrm{Spec}(R)/\mathfrak{g}[1]$.
nodes.statement_short: By Theorem 3.28, Spec(C) is the quotient by g[1].

nodes.name: Induced action
nodes.statement: As in the case of the usual group actions (one can work it out on the level of rational points), we get the induced action of $\mathbb{D}$ on $\mathrm{Spec}(C)$ (since $\mathfrak{g}[1]$ is normal in $\mathfrak{g}$) giving $(1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Normality of g[1] gives an induced action, proving (1).

nodes.name: Quotient group action
nodes.statement: For $(2)$, a similar argument gives a natural action of $\mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{g}[1]$ on $\mathrm{Spec}(C)$. By Remark \ref{gm}, we have $$\mathfrak{g}[m-1]^{\mathrm{Fr}}\cong \mathfrak{g}/\mathfrak{g}[1],$$ which proves $(2)$.
nodes.statement_short: g/g[1] ≅ g[m-1]^{Fr} acts, proving (2).

nodes.name: Reduce to e.c. fields
nodes.statement: We consider the theory of $\mathfrak{g}$-fields as a universal theory in the language of $\mathfrak{g}$-fields (containing $-$ and $\div$). Then any $\mathfrak{g}$-field embeds into an existentially closed $\mathfrak{g}$-field. Therefore, it is enough to prove that existentially closed $\mathfrak{g}$-fields are strict, so we may assume that $\mathbf{K}$ is existentially closed.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices that existentially closed g-fields are strict.

nodes.name: Non-strict constant a
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathbf{K}$ is not strict, i.e. there is $a\in K\setminus K^p$ which is a constant of $\mathbf{K}$. To reach a contradiction (with the assumption that $\mathbf{K}$ is existentially closed), it is enough to find a $\mathfrak{g}$-extension $\mathbf{K}\subseteq \mathbf{L}$ such that $a^{1/p}\in L$. Let $C$ denote the field of constants of $\mathbf{K}$ and $B$ be a $p$-basis of $C$ over $K^p$ such that $a\in B$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a constant a not a p-th power; aim to adjoin a^{1/p}; choose a p-basis B of C over K^p containing a.

nodes.name: Claim 1 block
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 1} \\ There is a $\mathfrak{g}[m-1]$-derivation on $C^{1/p}$ extending the one we have on $K$ and such that for each $b\in B$ and each $\mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}$, we have $$D_{\mathbf{j}}(b^{1/p})=(D_{p\mathbf{j}}(b))^{1/p}.$$ \begin{proof}[Proof of Claim 1] By Lemma \ref{deronc}(2) and Remark \ref{dpidpj}, $$\mathbb{D}':=\left(D_{p\mathbf{j}}|_C\right)_{\mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}}$$ is a $\mathfrak{g}[m-1]^{\mathrm{Fr}}$-derivation on $C$. Let $\mathrm{Fr}_C^{-1}:C\cong C^{1/p}$, and $\mathbb{D}''$ be $\mathbb{D}'$ transported to $C^{1/p}$ using $\mathrm{Fr}_C^{-1}$. Then $\mathbb{D}''$ is a $\mathfrak{g}[m-1]$-derivation on $C^{1/p}$ and by the construction it has the required properties (see also Lemma \ref{transport} and the proof of Proposition \ref{strictext}). \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Claim 1 and its proof.

nodes.name: Rings R and R'
nodes.statement: We consider the following rings (the set $B$ indexes the variables): $$R:=K\left[X_b^{(\mathbf{i})}\ |\ \mathbf{i}\in [p^m]^{\times e},\ b\in B\right],$$ $$R':=K\left[X_b^{(\mathbf{j})}\ |\ \mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e},\ b\in B\right];$$ where for each $b\in B$, $X_b$ is identified with $X_b^{(0,\ldots,0)}$. We put a $\mathfrak{g}$-ring structure on $R$ which is $\mathfrak{g}$-extending $\mathbf{K}$ in the following way: $$D_{\mathbf{j}}\left(X_b^{(\mathbf{i})}\right):=\sum_{\mathbf{f}\in [p^m]^{\times e}}c^{\mathbf{f}}_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}X_b^{(\mathbf{f})}.$$ Then $R'$ is a $\mathfrak{g}[m-1]$-subring of $R$.
nodes.statement_short: Define polynomial g-ring R over K and its g[m-1]-subring R'.

nodes.name: W, Psi and m
nodes.statement: Let us define a subset $W\subset R'$ as follows: $$W:=\left\{\left(X_b^{(\mathbf{j})}\right)^p-D_{p\mathbf{j}}(b)\ |\ \mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e},\ b\in B\right\}.$$ We define the following $K$-algebra map $$\Psi:R'\to C^{1/p},\ \ \Psi\left(X_b^{(\mathbf{j})}\right)=D_{p\mathbf{j}}(b)^{1/p}$$ and let $\mathfrak{m}=\ker(\Psi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define relations W, the map Ψ: R' -> C^{1/p} and m = ker Ψ.

nodes.name: m is a maximal g[m-1]-ideal
nodes.statement: By Claim 1, $\Psi$ is a $\mathfrak{g}[m-1]$-map, so $\mathfrak{m}$ is a maximal $\mathfrak{g}[m-1]$-ideal of $R'$ containing $W$.
nodes.statement_short: By Claim 1, m is a maximal g[m-1]-ideal containing W.

nodes.name: Goal: J prime
nodes.statement: We will show that the $\mathfrak{g}$-ideal $J$ in $R$ which is $\mathfrak{g}$-generated by $\mathfrak{m}$ is prime (then we can take $L$ as the field of fractions of $R/J$).
nodes.statement_short: It remains to show the g-ideal J generated by m is prime.

nodes.name: Orderings
nodes.statement: Let us order the set $[p^{m-1}]^{\times e}$ as $\mathbf{k}_{(1)},\ldots,\mathbf{k}_{(p^{(m-1)e})}$ such that for $i\leqslant j$, we have $|\mathbf{k}_{(i)}|\leqslant |\mathbf{k}_{(j)}|$ (in particular $\mathbf{k}_{(1)}=(0,\ldots,0)$). We also order $B=(b_s)_{s<\kappa}$ such that $b_0=a$.
nodes.statement_short: Order the index set by total degree and B with b_0=a.

nodes.name: Claim 2 block
nodes.statement: {\bf Claim 2} \\ There is a set of generators of $\mathfrak{m}$ consisting of elements of the following two types: $$\left(X_b^{(\mathbf{j})}\right)^p-D_{p\mathbf{j}}(b),\ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ \ X_{b_s}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(j)})} - \sum_{i=1}^{j-1}\sum _{l=0}^{p-1}\alpha_{t,i,l}\left(X_{b_s}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(i)})}\right)^l - \sum_{t<s}\sum_{\mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}}\beta_{t,\mathbf{j}}X_{b_t}^{(\mathbf{j})};$$ where $b\in B$, $s<\kappa$, $\mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}$, $j\in \{1,\ldots,p^{(m-1)e}\}$ and $\alpha_{i,l},\beta_{t,\mathbf{j}}\in K$. \begin{proof}[Proof of Claim 2] We construct a required set of generators in $p^{(m-1)e}\cdot \kappa$ steps. In Step (0,1), we add $X^p-b_0$ to the (so far empty) set of generators. In Step (0,2), we consider two cases. \\ Case 1: $D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0)\notin K^p(b_0)$. \\ In this case, we add the element $$\left(X_{b_0}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(2)})}\right)^p-D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0)$$ to the set of generators. \\ Case 2: $D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0)\in K^p(b_0)$. \\ In this case $$D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0)=\sum_{l=0}^{p-1}\alpha_l^pb_0^l,$$ for some $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{p-1}\in K$, and we add the element $$X_{b_0}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(2)})}-\sum_{l=0}^{p-1}\alpha_l^pX_{b_0}^l$$ to the set of generators. In Step (0,3), we proceed as in Step (0,2) with the field $K^p(b_0,D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0))$ replacing the field $K^p(b_0)$. Continuing like this, after $p^{(m-1)e}$ steps we obtain our desired set of generators for $b_0$. We continue in a similar way (although e.g. Step (1,1) already consist of two cases) for $(b_i)_{i>0}$. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Claim 2 and its proof.

nodes.name: Reduce operators
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{hsideal}, it is enough to apply to the generators from Claim 2 the operators $D_{\mathbf{i}}$, where $\mathbf{i}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}$ or where $\mathbf{i}$ is of the form $(p^{m-1})_i$ (see Lemma \ref{hsideal} for the definition of $(p^{m-1})_i$). If $\mathbf{i}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}$ then we get elements of $\mathfrak{m}$, so we may focus on the other case.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 3.33 only a few operators need to be applied to the generators.

nodes.name: First type of generators
nodes.statement: To treat the first type of the generators from Claim 2, we just need to use that there is $\mathbf{l}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}$ such that $\mathbf{i}=p\mathbf{l}$. We obtain the following: \begin{IEEEeqnarray*}{rCl} D_{p\mathbf{l}}\left(\left(X_b^{(\mathbf{j})}\right)^p-D_{p\mathbf{j}}(b)\right) & = & \left(D_{\mathbf{l}}\left(X_b^{(\mathbf{j})}\right)\right)^p-D_{p\mathbf{l}}\left(D_{p\mathbf{j}}(b)\right) \\ & = & \left(\sum_{\mathbf{k}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}} c_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}^{\mathbf{k}}X_b^{(\mathbf{k})}\right)^p - \sum_{\mathbf{k}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}} (c_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}^{\mathbf{k}})^pD_{p\mathbf{k}}(b) \\ & = & \sum_{\mathbf{k}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}} \left(c_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}}^{\mathbf{k}}\right)^p\left(\left(X_b^{(\mathbf{k})}\right)^p-D_{p\mathbf{k}}(b)\right), \end{IEEEeqnarray*} where the second equality holds by Remark \ref{dpidpj}, since $b\in C$. Hence we get that $D_{p\mathbf{l}}((X_b^{(\mathbf{j})})^p-D_{p\mathbf{j}}(b))$ belongs to the ideal generated by $W$ in $R'$, so it also belongs to $\mathfrak{m}$.
nodes.statement_short: Operators map p-th power generators into the ideal generated by W.

nodes.name: Second type of generators
nodes.statement: After applying $D_{\mathbf{i}}$ to the second type of generators, by Lemma \ref{newton} we get the following: $$D_{\mathbf{i}}\left( X_{b_s}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(j)})} - \sum_{i=1}^{j-1}\sum_{l=0}^{p-1}\alpha_{i,l}\left(X_{b_s}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(i)})}\right)^l - \sum_{t<s}\sum_{\mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}}\beta_{t,\mathbf{j}}X_{b_t}^{(\mathbf{j})} \right) = $$ $$ {\mathbf{k}_{(j)}+\mathbf{i}\choose \mathbf{i}}X_{b_s}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(j)}+\mathbf{i})} + \sum_{i=1}^{j-1}\sum_{l=0}^{p-1}d_{i,l}\left(X_{b_s}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(i)}+\mathbf{i})}\right)^l + Q,$$ for some $d_{i,l}\in K$, where $${\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}\choose \mathbf{i}}:={i_1+j_1 \choose i_1}\cdot \ldots \cdot {i_e+j_e \choose i_e},$$ and where $$Q\in K\left[X_{b_t}^{(\mathbf{r})},\ X^{(\mathbf{j})}_{b_s}\ |\ t<s,\ \mathbf{r}\in [p^m]^{\times e},\ \mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}\right].$$
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.14 gives a leading term with nonzero binomial coefficient.

nodes.name: Triangular generators of J
nodes.statement: We forget now about the HS-differential structure on $R$ and $J$. The obtained set of generators of $J$ is of the form $J_1\cup J_2$, where $J_1\subseteq \mathfrak{m}$ and $J_2\subseteq R'[X_{\gamma}]_{\gamma\in \mathcal{I}}$ (after renaming variables), and $$\mathcal{I}:=\kappa\times \{1,\ldots,e\}\times (\mathbf{k}_{i})_{i\in \{1,\ldots,p^{(m-1)e}\}}$$ with the lexicographical order. Moreover, there is a subset $\mathcal{I}_0\subset \mathcal{I}$ such that without loss of generality (since $p$ does not divide ${\mathbf{k}_{(j)}+\mathbf{i}\choose \mathbf{i}}$), we have $$J_2=\{X_{\gamma}-Q_{\gamma}\ |\ \gamma\in \mathcal{I}_0\},$$ where for each $\gamma\in \mathcal{I}_0$, $Q_{\gamma}\in R'[X_{\delta}]_{\delta<\gamma}$.
nodes.statement_short: J is generated by m and triangular relations X_γ - Q_γ.

nodes.name: J is prime
nodes.statement: Therefore, the ring $R/J$ is isomorphic to a polynomial ring over $R'/\mathfrak{m}$, so the ideal $J$ is prime.
nodes.statement_short: R/J is a polynomial ring over R'/m, so J is prime.

nodes.name: Derivation on C
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{deronc}(2) and Remark \ref{dpidpj}, $$\mathbb{D}':=\left(D_{p\mathbf{j}}|_C\right)_{\mathbf{j}\in [p^{m-1}]^{\times e}}$$ is a $\mathfrak{g}[m-1]^{\mathrm{Fr}}$-derivation on $C$.
nodes.statement_short: (D_{pj}) restricted to C is a g[m-1]^{Fr}-derivation.

nodes.name: Transport to C^{1/p}
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{Fr}_C^{-1}:C\cong C^{1/p}$, and $\mathbb{D}''$ be $\mathbb{D}'$ transported to $C^{1/p}$ using $\mathrm{Fr}_C^{-1}$. Then $\mathbb{D}''$ is a $\mathfrak{g}[m-1]$-derivation on $C^{1/p}$ and by the construction it has the required properties (see also Lemma \ref{transport} and the proof of Proposition \ref{strictext}).
nodes.statement_short: Transport via inverse Frobenius gives the required g[m-1]-derivation.

nodes.name: Transfinite construction
nodes.statement: We construct a required set of generators in $p^{(m-1)e}\cdot \kappa$ steps.
nodes.statement_short: Build the generators in p^{(m-1)e}·κ steps.

nodes.name: Step (0,1)
nodes.statement: In Step (0,1), we add $X^p-b_0$ to the (so far empty) set of generators.
nodes.statement_short: Start with X^p - b_0.

nodes.name: Step (0,2)
nodes.statement: In Step (0,2), we consider two cases.
nodes.statement_short: Split on membership of the next value.

nodes.name: Case 1
nodes.statement: Case 1: $D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0)\notin K^p(b_0)$. \\ In this case, we add the element $$\left(X_{b_0}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(2)})}\right)^p-D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0)$$ to the set of generators.
nodes.statement_short: If not in K^p(b_0), add a p-th power relation.

nodes.name: Case 2
nodes.statement: Case 2: $D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0)\in K^p(b_0)$. \\ In this case $$D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0)=\sum_{l=0}^{p-1}\alpha_l^pb_0^l,$$ for some $\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{p-1}\in K$, and we add the element $$X_{b_0}^{(\mathbf{k}_{(2)})}-\sum_{l=0}^{p-1}\alpha_l^pX_{b_0}^l$$ to the set of generators.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise add a linear relation.

nodes.name: Step (0,3)
nodes.statement: In Step (0,3), we proceed as in Step (0,2) with the field $K^p(b_0,D_{p\mathbf{k}_{(2)}}(b_0))$ replacing the field $K^p(b_0)$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat with the enlarged field.

nodes.name: Finish construction
nodes.statement: Continuing like this, after $p^{(m-1)e}$ steps we obtain our desired set of generators for $b_0$. We continue in a similar way (although e.g. Step (1,1) already consist of two cases) for $(b_i)_{i>0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Continue for all steps and all b_i.

nodes.name: Generalize to schemes
nodes.statement: It is convenient to show a more general result. Assume that $V,W$ are schemes over $k$ and $\mathbb{D}_V$ and $\mathbb{D}_W$ are $\mathfrak{g}$-derivations on $V$ and $W$ respectively.
nodes.statement_short: Work with g-schemes V and W.

nodes.name: Diagonal action
nodes.statement: As in the case of the usual group actions, we get a unique $\mathfrak{g}$-derivation on $V\times W$ such that the projections $V\times W\to V,W$ are $\mathfrak{g}$-invariant.
nodes.statement_short: The product carries a unique compatible action.

nodes.name: Dualize
nodes.statement: By considering the affine schemes and dualizing, we get what we need.
nodes.statement_short: Dualize for affine schemes.

nodes.name: Separably closed L_i
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{etalegext}, we can assume that $L_1,L_2$ are separably closed (since separable algebraic extensions are \'{e}tale). Then $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is a subfield of $L_1$ and $L_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to separable closures of L_1, L_2.

nodes.name: K^sep strict
nodes.statement: By Remark \ref{defgen}(5), it is a $\mathfrak{g}$-subfield. By Lemma \ref{constantdisjoint} (using Corollary \ref{dimconstants}), the $\mathfrak{g}$-field structure on $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ is strict. Therefore we can assume that $K$ is separably closed as well.
nodes.statement_short: K^sep is a strict g-subfield, so assume K separably closed.

nodes.name: Follow Ziegler
nodes.statement: The proof will be finished exactly as in \cite[Prop. 2.6]{Zieg2}. We can assume that $L_1,L_2$ are subfields of a big field $\Omega$ and that they are algebraically disjoint over $K$.
nodes.statement_short: Place L_1, L_2 algebraically disjoint in a big field.

nodes.name: Regularity
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{constantdisjoint}, the extension $K\subseteq L_1$ is separable. Since $K$ is separably closed, this extension is regular (see \cite[p. 367]{lang2002algebra}).
nodes.statement_short: K ⊆ L_1 is separable, hence regular.

nodes.name: Tensor product is a domain
nodes.statement: By \cite[Thm. VIII 4.12]{lang2002algebra}, $L_1$ and $L_2$ are linearly disjoint over $K$, thus $L_1\otimes_KL_2$ is a domain.
nodes.statement_short: Linear disjointness makes L_1⊗L_2 a domain.

nodes.name: g-structure on tensor product
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{forap}, there is a $\mathfrak{g}$-structure on $L_1\otimes_KL_2$ extending those on $L_1$ and $L_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.36 gives a g-structure on L_1⊗L_2.

nodes.name: Fraction field
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{etalegext} again, we get the required $\mathfrak{g}$-structure on the field of fractions of $L_1\otimes_KL_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Extend to the fraction field.

nodes.name: Delon's criterion
nodes.statement: By the proof of \cite[Theorem 2.1]{Del1} and by \cite[Claim 2.2]{Del1}, the extension $K\subseteq L$ is elementary if and only if $K$ and $L$ have the same (absolute) $p$-basis.
nodes.statement_short: Elementary iff same p-basis (Delon).

nodes.name: Étale criterion
nodes.statement: By \cite[Theorem 26.7]{mat}, it happens if and only if this extension is \'{e}tale, so we get the equivalence of $(1)$, $(2)$ and $(3)$.
nodes.statement_short: Same p-basis iff étale (Matsumura).

nodes.name: Definability of operators
nodes.statement: Since both the $\lambda$-function and the $\mathfrak{g}$-derivation are defined (over the field of the $p^m$-th powers) using the field operations and the elements of a $p$-basis, we get the equivalence of $(3)$ with $(4)$ and $(5)$.
nodes.statement_short: λ and the g-derivation are definable from a p-basis.

nodes.name: Canonical model
nodes.statement: We take the canonical $F$-derivation $\mathbb{D}^F$ on the field $K$ from Example \ref{canex}.
nodes.statement_short: Take the canonical F-derivation on k((X)).

nodes.name: Strict of degree e
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{canstrict}, $\mathbf{K}$ is strict and clearly the imperfection degree of $K$ is $e$.
nodes.statement_short: It is strict of imperfection degree e.

nodes.name: Extend to separable closure
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{etalegext}, $\mathbb{D}^F$ extends to the separable closure of $K$ (a separable algebraic extension is \'{e}tale, see \cite[Thm. 26.7]{mat}).
nodes.statement_short: Extend to the separable closure.

nodes.name: Still strict
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{constantdisjoint}(3), this extension is still strict. Since it is \'{e}tale, the degree of imperfection does not change.
nodes.statement_short: Strictness and imperfection degree are preserved.

nodes.name: K a field
nodes.statement: By Remark \ref{defgen}(1), Proposition \ref{etalegext} and Lemma \ref{lamb}(3), we can assume that $K$ is a field.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to K a field.

nodes.name: K strict
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lamb}(1), we have $K^p=L^p\cap K$. Since $\mathbf{L}\models \mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}_{\lambda}$, $\mathbf{L}$ is strict and hence $\mathbf{K}$ is strict as well.
nodes.statement_short: K is strict as a λ-substructure of strict L.

nodes.name: Amalgamate
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{lambdaap} and Lemma \ref{lamb}(2), we can $L^{\lambda}_{e,m}$-amalgamate $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{L}$ over $\mathbf{K}$ into a strict $\mathfrak{g}$-field $\mathbf{F}'$.
nodes.statement_short: Amalgamate F and L into strict F'.

nodes.name: Embed into elementary extension
nodes.statement: Since the extension $L\subseteq F'$ is separable, by \cite[Claim 2.2]{Del1} there is an elementary extension in the language of fields $L\preccurlyeq L'$ and a field embedding $\Upsilon:F'\to L'$ over $L$. The situation is described in the following diagram: \begin{equation*} \xymatrixcolsep{4pc} \xymatrix{ & & L'\\ & \mathbf{F}'\ar[ru]^{\Upsilon} & \\ \mathbf{F}\ar[ru]^{} & & \mathbf{L}\ar[lu]^{} \ar[uu]^{\preccurlyeq}\\ & \mathbf{K}\ar[ru]^{}\ar[lu]^{}. & } \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Embed F' into an elementary field extension L' of L.

nodes.name: L' étale over L
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{elementaryetale}, the extension $L\subseteq L'$ is \'{e}tale.
nodes.statement_short: L ⊆ L' is étale.

nodes.name: Imperfection bound
nodes.statement: The $\mathfrak{g}$-field $\mathbf{F}'$ is strict, so by Corollary \ref{dimconstants}, we have $[F':(F')^p]\leqslant p^e$.
nodes.statement_short: Strictness bounds [F':F'^p] by p^e.

nodes.name: Étale extensions
nodes.statement: Since the extension $L\subseteq F'$ is separable and $[L:L^p]=p^e$, by the equivalence between $(1)$ and $(2)$ in Lemma \ref{elementaryetale}, the extension $L\subseteq F'$ is \'{e}tale. Then the extension $F'\subseteq L'$ is \'{e}tale as well.
nodes.statement_short: L ⊆ F' and F' ⊆ L' are étale.

nodes.name: Extend derivation to L'
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{etalegext}, there is a $\mathfrak{g}$-derivation on $L'$ extending the one on $F'$ (hence also extending the one on $L$).
nodes.statement_short: Extend the g-derivation to L'.

nodes.name: Elementarity
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{elementaryetale}, the extension $\mathbf{L}\subseteq \mathbf{L}'$ is $L^{\lambda}_{e,m}$-elementary and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: L ⊆ L' is L^λ_{e,m}-elementary.

nodes.name: QE criterion
nodes.statement: For $(1)$, we use the criterion from \cite[Theorem 13.1]{sacks} (and Proposition \ref{elemamal}) exactly as in \cite[3.1]{Zieg2}.
nodes.statement_short: QE by Sacks' criterion with Proposition 4.4.

nodes.name: Strict F
nodes.statement: For $(2)$, let us take any $\mathfrak{g}$-field $\mathbf{F}$. By Proposition \ref{gstrictexist}, we may assume that $\mathbf{F}$ is strict.
nodes.statement_short: Take a g-field and make it strict.

nodes.name: Model of g-DCF_λ
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{consistent}, there is $\mathbf{L}\models \mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}_{\lambda}$. Clearly, $k$ with the trivial $\mathfrak{g}$-structure is a common $L^{\lambda}_{e,m}$-substructure of both $\mathbf{F}$ and $\mathbf{L}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a model L and the common substructure k.

nodes.name: Embedding
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{elemamal}, $\mathbf{F}$ embeds into an elementary extension of $\mathbf{L}$, which is clearly a model of $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}_{\lambda}$ as well.
nodes.statement_short: F embeds into an elementary extension of L.

nodes.name: Model completeness of g-DCF
nodes.statement: By $(1)$, $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}_{\lambda}$ is model complete, so using Lemma \ref{lamb}(2) and Lemma \ref{elementaryetale}, we get that $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$ is model complete as well.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer model completeness to g-DCF.

nodes.name: Model companion
nodes.statement: By $(2)$, $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$ is a model companion of the theory $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DF}$, so we get $(3)$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine to get (3).

nodes.name: Model completion
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{lambdaap} and the item $(1)$, we get $(4)$.
nodes.statement_short: Amalgamation plus QE gives (4).

nodes.name: Reduce to C^{1/p}
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be the field of constants of $\mathbf{K}$. It is enough to show that there is a unique $F$-derivation $\mathbb{D}'$ on $C^{1/p}$ extending $\mathbb{D}$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to extend D uniquely to C^{1/p}.

nodes.name: C is an F-subfield
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{deronc}(1), $C$ is an $F$-subfield of $K$.
nodes.statement_short: C is an F-subfield by Lemma 3.31(1).

nodes.name: Forced definition
nodes.statement: For $\mathbf{i}\in {\mathds{N}}^e$ and $a\in C^{1/p}$, we have the only option (as in \cite[Lemma 2.4]{Zieg2}): $$D'_{\mathbf{i}}(a):=(D_{p\mathbf{i}}(a^p))^{1/p}.$$ Clearly, each $D'_{\mathbf{i}}$ extends $D_{\mathbf{i}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Define D'_i(a)=D_{pi}(a^p)^{1/p}, the only option.

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: We need to show that $\mathbb{D}'=(D'_{\mathbf{i}})_{\mathbf{i}\in {\mathds{N}}^e}$ is an $F$-derivation.
nodes.statement_short: Show D' is an F-derivation.

nodes.name: Identify truncation
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{deronc}(2), the sequence of maps $$\mathbb{D}'':=(D_{p\mathbf{i}}(b))_{\mathbf{i}\in [p^m]^e}$$ is an $F[m-1]^{\mathrm{Fr}}$-derivation on $C$. It is easy to see that $\mathbb{D}'[m-1]$ coincides with $\mathbb{D}''$ ``transported'' to $C^{1/p}$ using the ring isomorphism $\mathrm{Fr}^{-1}_C:C\to C^{1/p}$.
nodes.statement_short: D'[m-1] is the transport of an F[m-1]^{Fr}-derivation on C.

nodes.name: Transport lemma
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{transport}, $\mathbb{D}'[m-1]$ is an $F[m-1]$-derivation.
nodes.statement_short: Hence D'[m-1] is an F[m-1]-derivation.

nodes.name: All m
nodes.statement: Since it happens for all $m\in {\mathds{N}}$, we get that $\mathbb{D}'$ is an $F$-derivation.
nodes.statement_short: Holds for every m, so D' is an F-derivation.

nodes.name: Local parameters form a p-basis
nodes.statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_e\in \mathcal{O}_G$ be a sequence of local parameters (see Example \ref{cangex}). By Example \ref{cangex}, \cite[30.6(ii)]{mat} and Proposition on page 276 of \cite{mat0}, $\{x_1,\ldots,x_e\}$ is a $p$-basis of $\mathcal{O}_G$, so it is also a $p$-basis of $k(G)$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Local parameters form a p-basis of O_G and k(G).

nodes.name: Finite separable
nodes.statement: Hence the field extension $k(x_1,\ldots,x_e)\subseteq k(G)$ is finite and separable.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Hence k(x) ⊆ k(G) is finite separable.

nodes.name: Generators and formulas
nodes.statement: Take $x_1,\ldots,x_e\in k(G)$ as in Lemma \ref{finsep}, denote $(x_1,\ldots,x_e)$ by $\mathbf{x}$ and let $y\in k(G)$ be separable algebraic over $k(\mathbf{x})$ such that $k(\mathbf{x},y)=k(G)$ (such $y$ exists by Lemma \ref{finsep} and Abel's theorem). Then for any $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}\in {\mathds{N}}^e$, there are polynomials $F_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}},H_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}\in k[\mathbf{X},Y]$ such that for the canonical $F$-derivation $\mathbb{D}^{F}=(D_{\mathbf{j}}^F)_{\mathbf{j}\in\mathbb{N}^e}$ on $k(G)$, we have $$D_{\mathbf{j}}^F(\mathbf{x}^{\mathbf{i}})=\frac{F_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{x},y)}{H_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{x},y)}\in k(G).$$
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Fix x, y generating k(G) and rational formulas for D^F_j(x^i).

nodes.name: Plan
nodes.statement: We describe now an extension by definitions of the theory $\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$ coinciding with the theory $G-\mathrm{DCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$. To ease the notation, we will also denote by $\mathbf{b}$ the tuple (of constant symbols or elements of a model) $(b_1,\ldots,b_e)$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Describe the definitional extension.

nodes.name: Defining axioms (♣)
nodes.statement: Take $\mathbf{j}=(j_1,\ldots,j_e)\in\mathbb{N}^e$, for every $n\geqslant \max\lbrace j_1,\ldots,j_e\rbrace$ we add to the theory $\mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$ the following defining axiom \begin{equation} \tag{$\clubsuit$} D_{\mathbf{j}}(x)=y \leftrightarrow \left(\exists^{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\; \alpha_{\mathbf{i}}\right) \left(x=\sum\limits_{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\alpha_{\mathbf{i}}^{p^n}\mathbf{b}^{\mathbf{i}} \;\wedge\; y=\sum\limits_{\mathbf{i}\in[p^n]^e}\alpha_{\mathbf{i}}^{p^n}\frac{F_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{b},c)}{H_{\mathbf{j},\mathbf{i}}(\mathbf{b},c)} \right). \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Add defining axioms for D_j via the p^n-power expansion in b.

nodes.name: Well-definedness
nodes.statement: Take any $(K,\mathbf{b},c)\models \mathrm{SCF}_{p,e}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$. It is not hard to verify that the defining axioms (\ref{scfD}) determine well-defined functions on $K$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: The axioms define functions on any model.

nodes.name: Copy of k(G)
nodes.statement: The axioms $\beta,\gamma$ guarantee that $$k(\mathbf{b},c)\cong_k k(G)$$ and that $\mathbb{D}:=(D_{\mathbf{j}})_{\mathbf{j}\in {\mathds{N}}^e}$ restricted to $k(\mathbf{b},c)$ corresponds to the canonical $G$-derivation on $k(G)$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: k(b,c) ≅ k(G) with the canonical G-derivation.

nodes.name: Étaleness
nodes.statement: Because $\mathbf{b}$ is a $p$-basis of $K$, the extension $k(\mathbf{b})\subseteq K$ is \'{e}tale (see \cite[Theorem 26.8]{mat}). Hence the extension $k(\mathbf{b},c)\subseteq K$ is also \'{e}tale.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: k(b,c) ⊆ K is étale.

nodes.name: Extend canonical derivation
nodes.statement: Due to Proposition \ref{etalehs}, we can extend the canonical $G$-derivation from $k(G)$ to the field $K$. Let $\mathbb{D}'=\left(D'_{\mathbf{j}}\right)_{\mathbf{j}\in\mathbb{N}^e}$ denote the $G$-derivation on $K$ extending the canonical $G$-derivation on $k(G)$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Extend the canonical G-derivation to K, call it D'.

nodes.name: Agreement
nodes.statement: Note that $D'_{\mathbf{j}}(x)=D_{\mathbf{j}}(x)$ for every $x\in K$, hence $\mathbb{D}'=\mathbb{D}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: D' agrees with the defined D.

nodes.name: Strict on k(b,c)
nodes.statement: Moreover the canonical $G$-derivation on $k(G)$ is strict, so also $\mathbb{D}'|_{k(\mathbf{b},c)}$ is strict.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: The canonical derivation is strict.

nodes.name: Model of G-DCF
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{constantdisjoint} implies that $\mathbb{D}'=\mathbb{D}$ is strict, so $(K,\mathbb{D},\mathbf{b},c)\models G-\mathrm{DCF}^{{\mathbf{b}},c}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 3.22, D is strict, giving a model of G-DCF^{b,c}.

nodes.name: Compose with isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $f\in Xk\llbracket X\rrbracket$ be an isomorphism between $F_1$ and $F_2$. For any $F_1$-derivation $\mathbb{D}:K\to K\llbracket X\rrbracket$, the following composition \begin{equation*} \xymatrix{K \ar[r]^{\mathbb{D}} & K\llbracket X\rrbracket \ar[r]^{\mathrm{ev}_f} & K\llbracket X\rrbracket} \end{equation*} is an $F_2$-derivation.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Composing with evaluation at the isomorphism f gives an F_2-derivation.

nodes.name: Triangular relation
nodes.statement: It is easy to see that for each positive integer $n$, there are $c_{n,1},\ldots,c_{n,n}\in k$ such that if $\mathbb{D}=(D_i)_{i\in {\mathds{N}}}$ then the corresponding $F_2$-derivation $\mathrm{ev}_f\circ \mathbb{D}$ is of the form $$(\mathrm{id},c_{1,1}D_1,c_{2,1}D_1+c_{2,2}D_2,\ldots),$$ hence the result follows.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: The new operators are triangular k-combinations of the old.

nodes.name: Good representative
nodes.statement: By \cite[Thm. 4.3]{HK2}, there is a formal group law $\widetilde{F}$ over $k$ such that $F\cong \widetilde{F}$ and the canonical $\widetilde{F}$-derivation restricts to $k[X]$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Find an isomorphic law whose canonical derivation restricts to k[X].

nodes.name: Replace F
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{isodef}, we can assume that $F=\widetilde{F}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.16 lets us replace F.

nodes.name: Repeat Theorem 4.14
nodes.statement: We can repeat now the proof of Theorem \ref{biin} (and we do not need to worry about the extra constant $c$).
nodes.section: 4.3 Bi-interpretability with a theory of separably closed fields
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the proof of Theorem 4.14.

nodes.name: Direction: e.c. implies axioms
nodes.statement: Assume that $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is an existentially closed $\mathfrak{g}$-field. Then by Proposition \ref{etalegext}, $K$ is separably closed (since a separable algebraic field extension is \'{e}tale). Take any $K$-irreducible $K$-varieties $V\subseteq \mathbb{A}^n$, $W\subseteq \nabla(V)$ and $Z\subsetneq W$. If $W$ projects generically onto $V$ then there is $b_0\in\Omega^n$ and $b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{p^{me}-1})\in\Omega^{np^{me}}$ such that $V=\mathrm{locus}_K(b_0)$ and $W=\mathrm{locus}_K(b)$. Since $c_V(W)\subseteq \nabla(W)$, Lemma \ref{cVW} implies that there exists a $\mathfrak{g}$-field extension $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq (K(b),\mathbb{D}')$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$. We have $$\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b\in W(K(b))\setminus Z(K(b))$$ and $b_0\in V(K(b))$. Since $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is existentially closed, there is $b_0'\in V(K)$ such that $\mathbb{D}_V(b'_0)\in W(K)\setminus Z(K)$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume K existentially closed and verify the axioms.

nodes.name: Separably closed
nodes.statement: Assume that $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is an existentially closed $\mathfrak{g}$-field. Then by Proposition \ref{etalegext}, $K$ is separably closed (since a separable algebraic field extension is \'{e}tale).
nodes.statement_short: An e.c. g-field is separably closed.

nodes.name: Generic points
nodes.statement: Take any $K$-irreducible $K$-varieties $V\subseteq \mathbb{A}^n$, $W\subseteq \nabla(V)$ and $Z\subsetneq W$. If $W$ projects generically onto $V$ then there is $b_0\in\Omega^n$ and $b=(b_0,\ldots,b_{p^{me}-1})\in\Omega^{np^{me}}$ such that $V=\mathrm{locus}_K(b_0)$ and $W=\mathrm{locus}_K(b)$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose generic points b_0, b of V and W.

nodes.name: Lemma 5.5
nodes.statement: Since $c_V(W)\subseteq \nabla(W)$, Lemma \ref{cVW} implies that there exists a $\mathfrak{g}$-field extension $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq (K(b),\mathbb{D}')$ such that $\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b$. We have $$\mathbb{D}'_V(b_0)=b\in W(K(b))\setminus Z(K(b))$$ and $b_0\in V(K(b))$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.5 gives a g-field extension realizing b.

nodes.name: Pull back to K
nodes.statement: Since $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is existentially closed, there is $b_0'\in V(K)$ such that $\mathbb{D}_V(b'_0)\in W(K)\setminus Z(K)$.
nodes.statement_short: Existential closedness yields a K-point.

nodes.name: Direction: axioms imply e.c.
nodes.statement: Assume now that $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is a model of the ``geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$'' and let $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq (L,\mathbb{D}')$ be an extension of $\mathfrak{g}$-fields. Take any quantifier-free formula $\varphi(x_0,\ldots,x_{p^{me}-1})$ over $K$ (in the language of fields), where each $x_i$ is an $n$-tuple of variables for an arbitrary (but fixed) positive integer $n$. Suppose that $(L,\mathbb{D}')\models (\exists x_0)\varphi(\mathbb{D}'(x_0))$. Take $b_0\in L^n$ such that $(L,\mathbb{D}')\models\varphi(\mathbb{D}'(b_0))$ and set $$V=\mathrm{locus}_K(b_0),\ \ b=\mathbb{D}_V'(b_0),\ \ W=\mathrm{locus}_K(b),\ \ Z_0=\lbrace d\in W\;\;|\;\; \neg\varphi(d)\rbrace.$$ Let $Z$ denote the intersection of all $K$-subvarieties of $W$ containing $Z_0$. Clearly $b\in W(L)\setminus Z(L)$ and the second condition of Lemma \ref{cVW} is satisfied, so $c_{V}(W)\subseteq \nabla(W)$. Hence all the assumptions of the ``geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$'' hold. Therefore there is $b_0'\in V(K)$ such that $\mathbb{D}(b_0')\in W(K)\setminus Z(K)$ and $(K,\mathbb{D})\models (\exists x_0)\varphi(\mathbb{D}(x_0))$.
nodes.statement_short: Assume the axioms and verify existential closedness.

nodes.name: Witness in extension
nodes.statement: Assume now that $(K,\mathbb{D})$ is a model of the ``geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$'' and let $(K,\mathbb{D})\subseteq (L,\mathbb{D}')$ be an extension of $\mathfrak{g}$-fields. Take any quantifier-free formula $\varphi(x_0,\ldots,x_{p^{me}-1})$ over $K$ (in the language of fields), where each $x_i$ is an $n$-tuple of variables for an arbitrary (but fixed) positive integer $n$. Suppose that $(L,\mathbb{D}')\models (\exists x_0)\varphi(\mathbb{D}'(x_0))$.
nodes.statement_short: Take a quantifier-free formula with a witness in an extension.

nodes.name: Varieties V, W, Z
nodes.statement: Take $b_0\in L^n$ such that $(L,\mathbb{D}')\models\varphi(\mathbb{D}'(b_0))$ and set $$V=\mathrm{locus}_K(b_0),\ \ b=\mathbb{D}_V'(b_0),\ \ W=\mathrm{locus}_K(b),\ \ Z_0=\lbrace d\in W\;\;|\;\; \neg\varphi(d)\rbrace.$$ Let $Z$ denote the intersection of all $K$-subvarieties of $W$ containing $Z_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Define V, W, Z from the witness.

nodes.name: Hypotheses of axioms
nodes.statement: Clearly $b\in W(L)\setminus Z(L)$ and the second condition of Lemma \ref{cVW} is satisfied, so $c_{V}(W)\subseteq \nabla(W)$. Hence all the assumptions of the ``geometric axioms for $\mathfrak{g}-\mathrm{DCF}$'' hold.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 5.5, c_V(W) ⊆ ∇(W), so the axioms apply.

nodes.name: Witness in K
nodes.statement: Therefore there is $b_0'\in V(K)$ such that $\mathbb{D}(b_0')\in W(K)\setminus Z(K)$ and $(K,\mathbb{D})\models (\exists x_0)\varphi(\mathbb{D}(x_0))$.
nodes.statement_short: The axioms give a witness in K.
